title: Colorado masonry company fires 30 workers who missed work for immigration protest; one calls the employer racist
text: The owner of a masonry business in Colorado is speaking publicly about his decision to fire more than 30 employees who did not come to work in support of last week's Day Without Immigrants protest. Jim Serowski, the owner of JVS Masonry, said in an interview with CNN on Sunday that he did nothing wrong. He said he had warned his employees about the consequences of joining the protest movement before they took the day off. Serowski said he told his employees, “If you're going to stand up for what you believe in you have to be willing to pay the price.” On Saturday, Serowski also spoke to his local CBS News affiliate in Denver after one employee alleged that his termination felt like racism. Serowski denied that the decision to terminate the workers was racially motivated in any way. He said he made the decision because the employees violated the company's policy on not showing up to work. He said the decision put his company in a difficult position, because he had to shut down two job sites on Thursday due to the protest, and the company now risks missing an important construction deadline. “They were told, if you no-call-no-show, you don't have a job,” Serowski told the news station. “It's that simple.”

title: Trump's Interior chief wants to carve up Utah's iconic Bears Ears monument!
text: It's happening. U.S. Interior Secretary Ryan Zinke said on Monday he has recommended that President Donald Trump shrink the Bears Ears National Monument in Utah – a move that instantly drew fire from furious conservationists while mining and drilling interests cheered it on. The vast 1.35 million acre (5,463 square kms) area, designated by former President Barack Obama in his final days in office and named for its iconic twin buttes, is the very first of 27 national monuments to face the Trump administration's review, part of a plan to ramp up development on federal lands. First on the chopping block! “My job is to make sure that I ... reflect the concerns of Utah, and reflect the concerns of the taxpayers and the public who own the lands, and I think we’ve done that,” Zinke told reporters in a teleconference about his interim recommendation, sent to Trump on Saturday. Zinke toured Utah for four days before making the call. His report argued that the Antiquities Act, used by past presidents to declare monuments, should cover only the “smallest area compatible” with protecting important sites. “Therefore... the Secretary of the Interior recommends that the existing boundary of the (Bears Ears) be modified to be consistent with the intent of the act.” Rather than designating a vast monument, as Obama did, “it would have been more appropriate to identify and separate the areas that have significant objects to be protected to meet the purposes of the Act,” Zinke's report said. So how much will be cut? More study is needed to decide how much smaller Bears Ears should be, Zinke said, and that decision will not come until all 27 monuments are reviewed.

title: Dead heat! Trump storms back to near-tie with Clinton after chaotic convention
text: The race just got tight. Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump has pulled nearly even with Democratic rival Hillary Clinton for the first time since May, according to a Reuters/Ipsos poll taken over the course of the Republican National Convention in Cleveland this week. The July 18-22 national online poll found 41 percent of likely voters backing Clinton and 38 percent backing Trump. With the poll's credibility interval of about 4 percentage points, the two should be considered about even. Just before Republicans opened the convention on Monday, Trump had trailed Clinton by nearly 10 percentage points. What a turnaround! The New York businessman-turned-politician formally accepted the Republican nomination for the Nov. 8 presidential election at a convention where the party at times struggled to show unity. The week opened with an ugly dustup between convention leaders and delegates who wanted to change the party's rules to derail Trump's nomination. Later, Senator Ted Cruz of Texas, who dropped out of the nomination race in May, flatly refused to endorse Trump in a prime-time speech. A public snub! Yet on the final night, Republicans gave Trump a standing ovation as he pledged to take back a country that he said is plagued by crime, terrorism and ineffective leadership. Party conventions are partly meant to introduce the candidate to the country, and nominees tend to get a boost in opinion polls afterward. In 2012, then-Republican nominee Mitt Romney rose by about 5 percentage points in the Reuters/Ipsos poll after his party's convention. Can Clinton strike back? She is expected to be formally nominated at her party's convention in Philadelphia next week, and she has led Trump most of the year in the poll.

text: U.S. Republican presidential nominee Donald Trump said on Tuesday that Democrat Hillary Clinton's plan for Syria would “lead to World War Three,” because of the potential for conflict with military forces from nuclear-armed Russia. Russia is a nuclear country, but a country where the nukes work as opposed to other countries that talk,” he said.

title: Fox News host proposes separate currency for non-white figures to keep Jackson on the $20 bill
text: Republicans have identified a new election-year wedge issue. After losing on Obamacare, marriage equality and Benghazi, the new source of anger they have identified is the placement of Harriet Tubman on the $20 bill. The matter is being treated as a major issue, and for Republicans it appears to amount to practically an attack on the Constitution itself. Many people on the right are objecting strongly to the plan to replace Jackson on the $20 bill. The change, however, is not new; it has been planned for a relatively long time. Opponents knew it was coming, and there was no outrage until it became clear that the replacement would be someone who was both non-white and non-male. Fox News host Greta Van Susteren proposed a response. Her plan is to leave white people's money as it is and to create separate money for non-whites. The proposal was not a joke: she said a new $25 bill should be made so that Jackson could remain in place. History offers a comparison. The government released a Susan B. Anthony dollar coin a long time ago, and it was disliked by everybody. It resembled a quarter, which confused people, and it was redundant, because there was already a $1 bill that the public was accustomed to. Not every cash register has room for a new bill slot, and certain types of automated bill-changing machines would also have to be retrofitted for a $25 bill. A new denomination of money would therefore be an annoyance and a hassle, and the public would not have patience for it.

title: Influence peddling scandal affects South Korean President Park
text: A South Korean court said on Sunday that it had issued arrest warrants for two former presidential aides who are under investigation in an influence peddling scandal that has pushed President Park Geun-hye's approval rating to a record low. Tens of thousands of South Koreans took part in a rally on Saturday evening in central Seoul, demanding that Park resign over the scandal. The scandal involves an old friend of the president, Choi Soon-sil, who is alleged to have used her closeness to Park to interfere in state affairs. Park's approval rating has fallen to 5 percent, the lowest since such polling began in 1988, according to a Gallup Korea survey released on Friday. The Seoul Central District Court said in a statement that it had granted prosecutors a warrant to arrest An Chong-bum, a former senior advisor to Park, who faces charges of abuse of power and attempted extortion. An was already in custody under an emergency detention order. Prosecutors are examining allegations that An and Choi forced South Korean conglomerates to donate funds to non-profit foundations. The court said it had also issued an arrest warrant for a second former presidential aide, Jeong Ho-seong, who had likewise already been held in temporary custody. Prosecutors detained Jeong late on Thursday on suspicion of leaking classified information. An and Jeong both resigned late last month as the crisis deepened.

title: Fox segment, one presidential speech, and a furious Sweden: how TV started a diplomatic mess
text: It started with a television segment. On Friday night, Fox News aired an alarming report in which host Tucker Carlson interviewed a documentary filmmaker about a crisis of violence in Sweden ignited by the recent wave of Muslim migration. “The government has gone out of its way to try to cover up some of these problems,” declared the filmmaker, Ami Horowitz. “That is grotesque,” Mr. Carlson responded. One viewer agreed. And in that moment a diplomatic incident was born – one that exposes the unusual way President Trump handles foreign policy, and how much television can shape his thinking. After watching the program, Mr. Trump tossed a line into a speech the next day suggesting that a terrorist attack had occurred in Sweden the night before. Just like that! No white papers, no intelligence reports, no interagency meeting and, presumably, no advice from his secretary of state. The president simply picked a fight with a longtime American friend, which resented his characterization and called it false. His only discernible goal? To make the case at home for his plans to restrict entry to the United States. The Swedes were stunned. “We are used to seeing the president of the U. S. as one of the most persons in the world, also well aware of the importance of what he says,” Carl Bildt, a former prime minister of Sweden, said by email on Monday. “And then, suddenly, we see him engaging in misinformation and slander against a truly friendly country, obviously relying on sources of a quality that at best could be described as dubious.” Aides scrambled to clarify that Mr. Trump's remarks were about a rising tide of crime in general, not any particular event or attack. But the president chose to escalate.

title: Photo of Obama in front of Che Guevara mural was more significant than it appeared
text: President Obama, a Nobel Peace Prize recipient, was photographed standing in front of a building that represents some of the worst oppression and human rights violations in the world. In the photo, Obama appears to be imitating a figure whom he likely regards as an icon. One of the first places visited on a government-sanctioned educational tour to Cuba several years ago was the Plaza de la Revolucion, a large expanse of concrete at the center of Havana that is less attractive than Tiananmen Square. It was there that President Obama was featured in the now-infamous photo in front of a giant mural of Che Guevara. The president lent his imprimatur to Guevara, a totalitarian who was responsible for the deaths of thousands. In some ways, however, the photo opportunity was worse than it looked. As the tour participants learned, the building that displays Guevara's face is home to the Cuban Ministry of the Interior. Unlike the Department of the Interior in the United States, Cuba's ministry is not charged with tasks such as protecting endangered waterfowl. Instead, it operates the National Revolutionary Police, which, in addition to keeping law and order on the streets, harasses and arrests dissidents and suppresses counter-revolutionary activities. It is, in effect, Cuba's version of the Stasi. During the trip, President Obama said that he was not going to tell Cubans to tear something down, a reference to President Reagan's exhortation to tear down the Berlin wall. Cuba, however, has no wall to tear down; it is separated from the rest of the world by ocean.

title: North Korean hackers behind WannaCry? Code clue points to notorious Lazarus gang!
text: A bombshell clue! On Monday, a Google security researcher announced he had found code in the “WannaCry” ransomware virus that suggests a notorious North Korean hacking group is behind the massive global cybercrime. Researcher Neel Mehta revealed the discovery in a cryptic Twitter message: 9c7c7149387a1c79679a87dd1ba755bc @ 0x402560, 0x40F598ac21c8ad899727137c4b94458d7aa8d8 @ 0x10004ba0, 0x10012AA4. What does it mean? As security firm Kaspersky explains, the message points to a block of code found both in an early version of the WannaCry virus – the far less harmful version that was later turbocharged into a global menace with stolen National Security Agency hacking tools – and in code obtained from a hacking group called Lazarus in 2015. In other words, this snippet is a “fingerprint” suggesting WannaCry was built by the Lazarus group. And Lazarus is no ordinary gang. It is associated with North Korea and has a long history of wantonly destructive behavior – most notoriously the attack on Sony Pictures Entertainment over the movie The Interview, which was seen as insulting to North Korean dictator Kim. “The scale of the Lazarus operations is shocking,” Kaspersky's Global Research Analysis Team warns. “The group has been very active since 2011 and was originally disclosed when Novetta published the results of its Operation Blockbuster research. During that research, which we also participated in, hundreds of samples were collected and show that Lazarus is operating a malware factory that produces new samples via multiple independent conveyors.” A malware factory! Kaspersky's report considers whether the code could be a “false flag,” planted deliberately by other hackers looking to frame Lazarus for the WannaCry attack – but concludes that scenario is “improbable.”

title: TV reporter fired after video shows her calling a police officer a “f***ing piece of s**t”
text: A television reporter has been fired after she was recorded on video directing an expletive-filled tirade at a Philadelphia police officer. She was asked to leave the club after multiple warnings for disrupting a show featuring comedian Craig Robinson with loud whispering. She allegedly then got into a fight with bar staff on the way out. F***ing piece of s**t. That's why nobody likes f***ing police in this f***ing town.” The officer then placed Campbell in handcuffs after she appeared to spit in the face of a man standing outside the club. She also took off her shoe and told the man to smell it. “What's that called? What's that called? Assault? Show me videotape,” Campbell said after she was handcuffed.

title: Obama declares war on wasted gas: sweeping crackdown on methane leaks from public land!
text: The gloves are off in the fight against climate change. On Friday, the Obama administration announced it will tear up 30-year-old regulations for oil and gas operations on public and tribal lands to stop the “wasteful release” of natural gas and slash methane emissions. The proposal by the Interior department's Bureau of Land Management would force oil and gas producers to use currently available technology to limit flaring at oil wells on federal land. Operators would also have to regularly check for natural gas leaks and replace outdated equipment that lets huge quantities of gas and methane escape into the air. And companies would finally get clarity on when they must pay royalties on flared natural gas. “These updated regulations, which would be phased in over several years ... would not only get more of our nation’s natural gas into pipelines and delivered to market but also reduce pollution and cut greenhouse gas emissions that are contributing to climate change,” Assistant Secretary for Land and Minerals Management Janice Schneider said. The BLM overhaul would only affect federal land. But the numbers are huge. Flaring would be cut by up to 60 percent and venting by up to 46 percent compared to 2013 rates. The BLM estimates it would prevent the loss of up to 56 billion cubic feet of gas a year through venting, flaring or leaks – enough to supply around 760,000 households annually! The agency said it would also avoid methane emissions equivalent to up to 4.2 million metric tons of carbon dioxide emissions per year.

title: Drowning in stuff? Marie Kondo's radical answer: choose joy!
text: This piece comes from Turning Points, a magazine that explores what the critical moments of this year might mean for the year ahead. The turning point: an executive at Ikea declared that the West has reached “peak stuff,” with people owning far too many things. Too much stuff! The Japanese word “tokimeku” means “to spark joy.” Anyone adopting my method of tidying must take a possession of hers and ask: “Does this spark joy for me?” That single question is the ONLY basis for deciding what to keep in one's home and what to throw out. But can this idea of sparking joy work on a much bigger scale? We live in a messy, chaotic world, much of it beyond our control. I read recently that more than 80 billion articles of clothing are produced every year – and only a negligible few are recycled. Staggering! As buying habits shift and technology moves almost everything to the cloud, people have started valuing experiences over material things. Some even say we may have hit a critical point in mass consumption – we have reached peak stuff. It can feel like our things are threatening to take over our world. But we can focus our energy and determination on choosing what makes us happy, and ultimately transform our lives. Asking whether something sparks joy sounds so simple that many people wonder whether it can really work. Yet the power of the “spark joy” standard lies precisely in its ambiguity. Let's consider, for argument's sake, more precise rules for what to keep or discard, even for something as basic as clothing. Should you own fewer than 10 jackets?

title: Rush Limbaugh, wife Kathryn, Sean Hannity and Ethel Kennedy attend Roger Ailes funeral under heavy security
text: Radio host and frequent Fox News contributor Laura Ingraham and Kimberly Guilfoyle, host of Fox News program The Five, were seen leaving the funeral service for former Fox News chief Roger Ailes with Sean Hannity. Guilfoyle was one of the few women at Fox News who supported Ailes when he was accused of sexual harassment by former Fox and Friends host Gretchen Carlson. Following his death, Guilfoyle posted a message of support for the Ailes family on Twitter on May 18, 2017: “RIP Roger Ailes sending my love and prayers to Beth & Zachary. Roger was a friend and a mentor to so many of us at Fox News he will be missed”. Guilfoyle also eulogized Ailes on Fox News. It was her current employers, the Murdoch sons, who fired Ailes, the man who brought Fox News to the top of the ratings, following allegations of sexual harassment by Gretchen Carlson and later by former Fox host Megyn Kelly. Ailes was eulogized in Palm Beach at St. Edward Roman Catholic church on Saturday morning in a service with many references to suffering. “Beth (Ailes' wife, Elizabeth) came to me Friday and asked that I officiate,” St. Edward Monsignor Thomas J. Klinzing said. “She asked me to base some of my reading on the theme of suffering. I believe Roger suffered quite a bit with those accusations.” Klinzing was referring to Ailes' dismissal last year from the network he founded, after former Fox News anchor Gretchen Carlson accused him of sexual harassment and other women came forward with similar accusations. Ailes' coffin was carried to the altar of the 90-year-old church at 11am.

title: Trump Justice Department says executive branch can withhold information from Democrats; senators from both parties object strongly
text: At the beginning of May, President Trump's Department of Justice issued an opinion that allows all government agencies to withhold information from Congressional Democrats, including Democrats who are the ranking members of their committees. The opinion was written so that Trump and the Justice Department can say it applies regardless of party, but that argument is a pretext. It states, in part: “Individual members of Congress, including ranking minority members, do not have the authority to conduct oversight in the absence of a specific delegation by a full house, committee, or subcommittee.” The opinion was written by acting Assistant Attorney General Curtis Gannon. It goes on to say: “They may request information from the Executive Branch, which may respond at its discretion, but such requests do not trigger any obligation to accommodate congressional needs and are not legally enforceable through a subpoena or contempt proceedings.” Under the opinion, individual members cannot subpoena certain information unless their committee chair does so. Ranking Democrats on Congressional committees will need their chairpersons to request information on their behalf. Rob Portman (R-Ohio) said that when he led the Office of Management and Budget under President George W. Bush, he considered it his responsibility to provide information to any member of Congress who requested it. Some of Trump's nominees, however, are declining to do so, even though they are being pressed on the matter in their confirmation hearings.

Trump told Fox News on Wednesday he was considering tapping former New York City Mayor Rudy Giuliani to lead a commission to study his proposed temporary ban on Muslims entering the United States! “We’ll figure it out and we will get it going, but we have to be extremely careful,” Trump said. His campaign admitted this month that several policy speeches are coming, after last month's address on his foreign policy views. In that April 27 speech in Washington, Trump offered few details – but vowed over and over to put America first! And he has effectively clinched the Republican Party's nomination for the Nov. 8 presidential election, as of last week!

title: What are they hiding? Oldest-ever nominees Trump, 70, and Clinton, 68, stay tight-lipped on health
text: They are the oldest pair of nominees in American history – and they are telling voters almost nothing about their health. Donald J. Trump and Hillary Clinton have been more secretive and selective than many recent presidential nominees about details of their personal health, a striking departure, experts say, given the candidates' age. No American election has ever featured two nominees as old as Mr. Trump, 70, and Mrs. Clinton, 68, and they have kept up a grueling pace for more than a year. Yet both have refused to share the latest information about their health or make their doctors available for interviews. Each released a brief medical statement in 2015 – and neither has added a word since. Mr. Trump has been especially tight-lipped, even as he tries to turn health into a campaign issue, questioning Mrs. Clinton's “physical and mental strength and stamina” while his allies push unfounded rumors that she is ill. Hope Hicks, a spokeswoman for Mr. Trump, said Monday that he would have “no problem releasing additional records” about his health if Mrs. Clinton did the same. Clinton's advisers, noting she has released more details than Mr. Trump, said the onus was on him to match her disclosures. Stalemate! It wasn't always like this. Republicans from Ronald Reagan to Mitt Romney released details in the months before Election Day or let their doctors field questions. John McCain allowed some reporters to review more than 1,100 pages of his medical records. Among Democratic nominees, Al Gore and John Kerry spoke openly about their health; Mr. Kerry had survived prostate cancer. Bill Clinton and Barack Obama were more reticent: their aides argued that the two were young men with no health problems, though Mr. Clinton granted an interview on his health in 1996 under pressure from his Republican opponent, Bob Dole.
